We first met when his book, On Courage: How to Be a Dissident in an Age of Fear, came out earlier this year. Ami is a senior fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School’s Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation and a former senior policy advisor at the White House. He views democracy issues through a broad lens, both internationally and domestically. So when he texted me, “Huge week on the authoritarianism front - Lula pushed back Bolsonaro 2.0 in Brazil, Serbia’s strongman just lost, and now headed into Israel and US…Perhaps a good week for us to get on a Substack live and chat about the anti-authoritarian tide?” I immediately said, “Yes!”

If all of that has your head spinning, or if you have been keeping up but would like to hear what an expert has to say about these developments, Ami joins us tonight, Monday, at 8 pm ET to discuss the international pushback against authoritarianism in some unexpected places, including the student-led movement in Serbia that has echoes of Indivisible in the U.S.

To get straight to the good part: the common thread is voter mobilization. That’s what led to good results for people who don’t want to live under authoritarian regimes in Brazil and Serbia. Israelis, who can’t vote from abroad, are flying home to cast ballots against Netanyahu in large numbers. We can do our part here too. Voting allows us to alter the course of history.

See you tonight—leave any questions you have for us here.
